steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Definition: Synthesis means combining information from different sources to create a summary. You draw together ideas from both texts to show common themes or differences. | Step 1: Read both texts and identify the key information Step 2: Decide what each text says about the topic Step 3: Find similarities and/or differences Step 4: Write in your own words, using brief quotations Step 5: Organise logically - group related points | Remember: In synthesis questions, don't analyse language devices. Focus on summarising what each text says about the topic. | Examiner's Tip: This is NOT a language analysis question. Focus on what each text SAYS - the content and ideas. Use your own words and keep quotations brief. Spend about 10 minutes on this question.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: What is the main difference between synthesis and comparison? | Should you analyse language devices in a synthesis question? | How should you use quotations in synthesis?
